---
title: "Reward Model"
description: "A learned model that scores outcomes or behavior according to a reward or preference signal."
term: "Reward Model"
letter: "R"
category: "Reinforcement Learning"
difficulty: "Advanced"
---

## Simple explanation

A reward model estimates how desirable an outcome or behavior is. It can
provide a learning signal when directly specifying a reward for every
possible situation is difficult.

## Technical explanation

A reward model maps a state, action, trajectory, or response to a scalar
score intended to approximate a target preference or reward. It may be
trained from demonstrations, ratings, or pairwise comparisons. In
preference-based language-model training, a model can learn to score
responses, but that score is only a proxy for human judgments.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Reward models are used in preference optimization, reinforcement learning,
and learned objectives. They can scale feedback, but may be exploited by
optimization, encode annotator biases, or fail outside the training
distribution.

## How it works

The model is trained on examples labeled with rewards or relative
preferences. A downstream optimizer or policy uses its scores to select
behavior. Evaluation should include held-out judgments, adversarial cases,
and checks that optimizing the reward does not degrade important properties.

## Practical example

Given pairs of assistant responses with a human preference label, a reward
model can learn to assign a higher score to the preferred response. A
language-model policy can then be optimized against that score, with
independent evaluation to catch reward hacking.

## Common misconceptions

- A reward-model score is not an objective measure of quality or safety.
- Optimizing a learned score can reveal weaknesses in the score model
  instead of improving the intended real-world behavior.
